players.comment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network. The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.
Prince (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans. Right knee soreness continues to plague Prince. The veteran forward's absence has a negligible impact on the Detroit rotation.

Caruso won't return to Wednesday's game against the Hawks due to right hip soreness, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. Caruso will end his evening with five points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one assist, one steal and two turnovers across nine minutes. For now, Caruso should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Pelicans.

Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports. Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

Capela (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Indiana. Capela is still recovering from a right ankle sprain and will remain on the inactive list for a ninth straight game. The veteran center's next opportunity to play will come Friday at Denver.

Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday. Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball. Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Allen (concussion-like symptoms) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers. With Allen on the shelf, Royce O'Neale and Christian Anderson should see a boost in minutes off the Hornets' bench. Allen's next chance to suit up will come Friday versus the Hawks.

Landale (hip) won't play Wednesday in Oklahoma City. This will be Landale's second straight game on the sidelines, which should help Zuby Ejiofor remain in the rotation. For now, Landale should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Hornets.

Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports. Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

Horford (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks, but will play Thursday against the Grizzlies, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports. Horford will miss the first half of a back-to-back set Wednesday due to a back injury, but will be available Thursday. Charles Bassey could see an expanded role in Horford's absence, while Horford could see a larger role than usual Thursday with Draymond Green set to rest.

Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports. Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis. This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Wade (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game in Orlando. With both Wade and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) out for Wednesday's game, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could draw a spot-start, and there will be more minutes available for Jabari Walker and Justin Edwards. Wade's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Bucks.

Brown (hamstring) will be re-evaluated at some point this weekend, per Kris Rihm of ESPN.com. It sounds like the 76ers are bracing for Brown, who is out for Wednesday's game against the Magic with a left hamstring strain, to be sidelined for multiple games. The star forward should be re-evaluated prior to Saturday's matchup versus the Bucks, and more usage should fall into the hands of Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and LeBron James for as long as Brown is on the shelf.

Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics. Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game in Cleveland. This will be Jerome's third straight game on the inactive list due to the hip injury, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Thursday's meeting with the Warriors. Cam Spencer should continue to start in his absence and Javon Small will have the chance for some extended minutes. Cedric Coward should continue to see some increased playmaking responsibilities with Jerome sidelined.

Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Head coach JJ Redick said Reaves' (heel) pregame workout went "well," but he remains without an official timetable to return, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports. Given that Reaves' workout went "well" and the injury has been classified as a "heel bruise," we'd take the "no timetable" comment from Redick with a grain of salt. For now, Reaves should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Kings.

Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

Barrett (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Wizards, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports. Grange adds that the star forward's hamstring was sore after Tuesday's game against the Knicks, prompting a cautious approach for the second half of Toronto's back-to-back. His absence takes a key scoring wing out of the lineup and puts more pressure on Immanuel Quickley at point guard, and Barrett figures to be replaced by Jamal Shead in the starting lineup.

Nembhard (hip) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Rockets, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. It will be the second consecutive absence for Nembhard, who has been battling a hip injury. However, head coach Rick Carlisle indicated the 26-year-old likely won't be out long, so the door is open for his potential return Friday versus the Cavaliers. With Nembhard sidelined again, Quenton Jackson will presumably remain in the starting lineup.

Head coach Rick Carlisle said Tuesday that Haliburton (hamstring) is "getting there," but there's still no definitive timetable for his return to game action, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports. Carlisle wouldn't rule out a return in November, though he added that there's "nothing happening in the near-term." The star point guard hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and until he's cleared to return, Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties while Quenton Jackson sees increased burn.

Williams (hamstring) has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated Saturday. Williams sustained a left hamstring strain in the Nov. 9 win over New Orleans, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Boston. LJ Cryer will likely continue seeing increased burn in Williams' stead.

Murphy (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit. The star forward is missing a sixth consecutive contest with bilateral knee tendinopathy. Saddiq Bey should remain rostered in all fantasy leagues while Murphy is on the shelf.
Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit. Watford will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a definitive return timeline.

Maxey (foot) is out for Wednesday's game in Orlando, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. Maxey will join Jaylen Brown (hamstring) on the inactive list for Wednesday's game, and it'll be Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope starting in their place. For now, Maxey should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Bucks.

Gardner (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks. Gardner was already in line to hit the bench in Pelle Larsson's (illness) return. He'll have some extra time to recover ahead of Sunday's showdown with the Thunder.

Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week. Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days. Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

Cunningham (knee) won't play in Wednesday's game against New Orleans. Cunningham logged 37 minutes in Tuesday's 105-93 win over the Spurs but won't play Wednesday due to knee soreness. He will presumably be back on the floor Friday against the Raptors. With Cunningham sidelined, Daniss Jenkins will likely have the ball in his hands more than usual. Paul Reed might also enter the starting lineup alongside Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, John Collins and Ausar Thompson.

Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports. Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks. Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports. Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

Stewart (illness) won't play Wednesday against the Cavs. This will be Stewart's second straight game on the sidelines, which should lead to more minutes for Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post. Stewart's next chance to play will come Thursday against the Warriors.

Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic. The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Barnes (injury management) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Washington, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports. Barnes will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set, though he'll likely be back for Friday's game at Detroit. With the star forward unavailable, Jakob Poeltl, Allen Graves and Jamison Battle are candidates for increased playing time. Moreover, Kyle Anderson could rejoin the rotation.

Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports. This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports. Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit. McGowens will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. It's unclear how far along he is in his recovery.

Watson (back) is out for Wednesday's game versus Memphis. Watson's next chance to play comes Friday against Indiana. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) ruled out, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas should each play significant minutes for Cleveland on Wednesday.

Rollins (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game at Miami. Rollins wasn't included on the initial injury report, though he's since been ruled out for a second straight game due to an illness. His next chance to play will come Thursday versus Portland. With the 24-year-old combo guard sidelined, Kasparas Jakucionis and Gary Trent will likely continue seeing increased minutes.

Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports. Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL. Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit. Mathurin will miss a third straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the short-handed Pelicans moving forward.
Lively (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Lively remains out indefinitely due to 2025 foot surgery. Meanwhile, Daniel Gafford is locked in as Dallas' top center.

Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Memphis. Tyson will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right ankle injury, and his next opportunity to play will come Friday against Indiana. With Peyton Watson (back) expected to join Tyson on the inactive list, there will be more minutes available for guys like Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas.

Holland (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans. Holland bruised his knee in the waning moments of Saturday's blowout loss in Miami. His next chance to end a two-game absence comes Friday against Toronto, with Kevin Huerter likely playing heavy minutes for Detroit in the meantime.

Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Barlow (back) is out for Wednesday's game against Orlando. Barlow will be re-evaluated later this week and is thought to be closing in on his season debut, but he's not ready for game action quite yet. His next chance to return from a stress reaction in his back comes Saturday versus the Bucks.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Sengun (eye) will not return to Wednesday's game against the Pacers, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports. Sengun exited the game in the second quarter after taking a shot to the face and will not be able to return. Steven Adams figures to see extra minutes in his absence.

Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns. Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports. Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis. Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks. Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports. Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

Murray-Boyles will not return to Wednesday's game against the Wizards due to an illness, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports. Murray-Boyles saw just four minutes of action before exiting due to an illness. Allen Graves and Kyle Anderson could see extra minutes with Murray-Boyles sidelined.

Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months. Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets. Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday. Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

Smith suffered a right ankle sprain during Wednesday's game against the Wizards, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Smith exited the game in the fourth quarter due to an apparent right ankle sprain. He concluded the game with eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and two steals in 18 minutes. His status for Friday's game against the Cavaliers is now in question.

Lawal is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors due to tightness in his right groin. It sounds like the rookie forward is dealing with a minor issue. His next chance to suit up comes Saturday against the Clippers.

Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies. Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Flemings (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder. Flemings is progressing well, having practiced Tuesday, but the Hawks are taking a cautious approach with the rookie first-round pick. With CJ McCollum on the shelf with a calf strain, Luguentz Dort is likely to enter the first unit while Aaron Wiggins takes on a larger role off the bench.

Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com. The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

Leonard (knee) has progressed in his strength and conditioning program but will miss at least one more week, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports. Leonard last played Oct. 23 due to left knee swelling but is seemingly nearing a return to action. The star forward will likely operate under a minutes restriction upon his return, but until then, Ja'Kobe Walter, Allen Graves and Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to see increased playing time.

Okpara (illness) is available for Friday's game against Toronto. Okpara will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up Friday. However, the two-way player isn't guaranteed to see the floor.
players.stale_reason: designation was for an earlier game
